reproduction: Run command_argv from the repository root after building bitcoind and bitcoin-sharepool-signer with native functional tests enabled.
stdout_and_stderr_redirect is the exact original output redirection. The commands are recorded as argv, without shell quoting.
Change --configfile to the generated test/config.ini of your local build, and choose unused temporary directories and port seeds.
Fresh native signer keys and varying wall-clock times produce different commitments. Reproduce the passing assertions, not identical random hashes or timings.
The tests overlapped and share local machine resources. Reported wall time is regression-test duration, not a throughput benchmark.
sanitization: Temporary test directory paths in successful logs are replaced with <TEST_TMPDIR>. The result JSON is copied unchanged. No signer secrets, RPC credentials, hardware configuration or failed-run logs are included.
limits: The 100-miner case uses 100 separate logical gates and signer keys, with one validating native node and one P2P follower; it does not use 100 native nodes.
All 100 independent valid transactions and 100 distinct native templates are checked. The collector admits all 100 proofs; full 100-by-100 replication between miner gates is not simulated.

At this deliberately easy regtest target, share PoW uses the maximum 256-bit target and unit work. The exact eight-network-work window spans 16 full shares and part of a 17th, so admission of 100 proofs does not imply all 100 recipients earn from that block.
Admission order is canonical native block order followed by increasing numeric proof ID within each block. It is not wall-clock receipt order; the window visits that ordering backwards.

A cutoff inside one large admission batch selects the largest numeric proof IDs first. These tests neither measure nor rule out withholding, proof selection or grinding advantages around that boundary.
The cases do not establish equal payout variance to a regular pool, mainnet proof sampling calibration, WAN latency, sustained capacity, data-availability resilience or adversarial fairness.

The miner gate checks its locally acknowledged work. Only work admitted into canonical pool history becomes recurring reward-eligible; a provisional local receipt is not an unconditional future payment guarantee.
The same recipient script can participate in different pools without an ownership signature; per-job pool and recipient bindings remain immutable.
The tiny-reward cases verify current builder behavior: no payout fix was needed because the normal witness commitment preserves a nonempty coinbase when all monetary payouts floor to zero.
